learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Ethics Scope and Competence.
Apply Ethics Scope and Competence to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: Professionals must work within competence, obtain informed consent, protect neural data and distinguish education, research and clinical diagnosis.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Medical EEG interpretation and seizure diagnosis require appropriately qualified practitioners. Commercial conflicts and persuasive visual outputs require extra transparency.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Protects clients from delayed medical care, false reassurance and expensive unsupported treatment.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Using “brain scan” language can imply diagnostic certainty the method does not provide.

quizBank.question: Which statement best captures Ethics Scope and Competence?
options: Professionals must work within competence, obtain informed consent, protect neural data and distinguish education, research and clinical diagnosis.
It provides a stand-alone psychiatric diagnosis
It is unaffected by state and artifact
Its interpretation requires no clinical context
quizBank.explanation: Professionals must work within competence, obtain informed consent, protect neural data and distinguish education, research and clinical diagnosis.

quizBank.question: What is the safest clinical principle for Ethics Scope and Competence?
options: Integrate raw signal quality, state, method and clinical context
Assume a coloured map shows exact anatomy
Treat statistical rarity as proof of disorder
quizBank.explanation: EEG and QEEG interpretation requires converging evidence, technical validity and clinical context.

quizBank.question: Which error is most important to avoid in Ethics Scope and Competence?
options: Using “brain scan” language can imply diagnostic certainty the method does not provide.
quizBank.explanation: Using “brain scan” language can imply diagnostic certainty the method does not provide.

reviewPrompts.answer: Medical EEG interpretation and seizure diagnosis require appropriately qualified practitioners. Commercial conflicts and persuasive visual outputs require extra transparency.
Protects clients from delayed medical care, false reassurance and expensive unsupported treatment.
Using “brain scan” language can imply diagnostic certainty the method does not provide.
Scope is part of science, not administrative decoration.
